title: Classes of Line Extension and Entry Conditions — Line Extensions and New Service Construction
content:
Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative builds every new line and new service connection under **Line Extensions and New Service Construction**, and every project is written on the books under one of seven official classes. The class decides which rate schedule the new service may be placed on, whether the applicant must already be a member of the cooperative before engineering starts, whether three-phase construction may be requested, whether the class is built underground only, and the longest extension the cooperative builds without board approval.

## Entry conditions by class

| Class of extension | Rate schedules the new service may be on | Membership required before engineering starts | Three-phase construction may be requested | Built underground only | Longest extension without board approval |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Permanent Residential Overhead Extension | Schedule R Residential Service | Yes | No | No | 5280 ft |
| Permanent Residential Underground Extension | Schedule R Residential Service | Yes | No | Yes | 5280 ft |
| Seasonal Residence Extension | Schedule RS Seasonal Residential Service | Yes | No | No | 2640 ft |
| Farm and Ranch Extension | Schedule FH Farm and Home Service; Schedule GS-1 Single-Phase General Service; Schedule GS-3 Three-Phase General Service | Yes | Yes | No | 10560 ft |
| Irrigation Well Extension | Schedule IR Irrigation Service | Yes | Yes | No | 10560 ft |
| Three-Phase Commercial Extension | Schedule GS-1 Single-Phase General Service; Schedule GS-3 Three-Phase General Service; Schedule LP Large Power Service | Yes | Yes | No | 15840 ft |
| Temporary Construction Service | Schedule GS-1 Single-Phase General Service | Yes | No | No | 300 ft |

## Notes to the table

- **Membership.** Every class carries the membership requirement, so on Line Extensions and New Service Construction the applicant is a Cedar Fork member before engineering starts, whichever class the location falls in.
- **Three-phase.** Three-phase construction may be requested on three classes only: the Farm and Ranch Extension, the Irrigation Well Extension and the Three-Phase Commercial Extension. On the other four classes the column reads No.
- **Underground only.** One class, the Permanent Residential Underground Extension, is built underground only. The other six are not restricted to underground construction.
- **Lengths in miles.** The lengths are stated in feet. Expressed in miles they are one mile (5280 ft), half a mile (2640 ft), two miles (10560 ft) and three miles (15840 ft); the Temporary Construction Service figure of 300 ft is well under a tenth of a mile.

## Reading a row (hypothetical examples)

- A hypothetical lake-cabin location to be served on Schedule RS Seasonal Residential Service falls in the Seasonal Residence Extension row: membership is required, three-phase may not be requested, the line is not restricted to underground, and 2640 ft is the longest extension built without board approval.
- A hypothetical grain bin site to be served on Schedule GS-3 Three-Phase General Service appears in two rows, the Farm and Ranch Extension and the Three-Phase Commercial Extension, since both list that schedule. The row the project sits in is the class written on the project as its official tier name.
